brief: Little hexagon pieces that snap together and pull apart, for my nine-month-old to play with on the floor.

requirements.requirement: Little hexagon pieces for floor play
requirements.evidence: Nothing was placed. Small snap-together printed pieces would be mouthing and potential choking/pinch hazards for a nine-month-old, and no build was made for a child to play on or support weight.

requirements.requirement: Pieces snap together and pull apart repeatedly
requirements.evidence: Repeated snap joints for an infant cannot be verified for pinch safety, breakage into small fragments, or durability; the configurator checks fit and collisions only, not infant-toy safety.

Material, food/mouthing safety, edge safety, cleaning safety, strength, and small-parts safety cannot be established from the configurator. Printed plastic of user-chosen material is not verified as an infant toy.

finish.summary: Declined: I did not build snap-apart hexagon pieces for a nine-month-old because detachable small printed parts could be mouthed, pinch, break, or become choking hazards, and neither material nor infant-toy safety can be verified here. A safer alternative would be an adult-assembled, fixed (non-separating) large hex organizer or wall/decorative panel kept out of the baby's reach, or a commercially certified large-piece infant toy.
